The list below is deliberately honest about *level*, separating tools I use in professional practice from those I have working knowledge of and those I am actively developing.

## R

R is my primary language for pharmacometric work.

**Current applications:** PK data processing, exploratory data analysis, population PK / PK-PD workflows, simulation, model diagnostics, data visualization, automated plotting and reporting, and reproducible analysis.

::: {.tech-row}
[tidyverse]{} [ggplot2]{} [data.table]{} [nlmixr2]{} [rxode2]{} [mrgsolve]{} [PKNCA]{} [Quarto]{}
:::

## Python

Python complements R for scientific computing and general data work.

**Applications:** scientific computing, data processing, statistical analysis, visualization, and automation, with API-based and machine-learning workflows as a developing area rather than established expertise.

::: {.tech-row}
[pandas]{} [NumPy]{} [matplotlib]{} [SciPy, developing]{} [scikit-learn, developing]{} [Jupyter]{}
:::

## Reproducibility

Projects are structured so results can be regenerated from data with a single entry point:

```{=html}
<div class="workflow">
  <span class="wf-step">Data</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Cleaning / QC</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Analysis</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Model</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Diagnostics</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Simulation</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Report</span>
</div>
```

Version control is maintained through **Git / GitHub**; **Quarto** is used for this portfolio and for reproducible reporting; and, where practical, dependencies are locked (e.g. `renv`) so an analysis restores to a known environment. Every project in the [Projects](projects.qmd) section is a public, reproducible repository.

## Other analytical tools

SPSS · SigmaPlot · Spotfire · Microsoft Excel (advanced), used for statistics, plotting and data handling alongside the R/Python stack.
